classification.difficultyReason: Choose an arrangement that maximises shared edges to minimise exposed perimeter.

content.prompt: Three square tiles have sides of length $1$ cm, $2$ cm and $3$ cm. These three squares are arranged without overlap to create a figure of minimum possible perimeter. Find the perimeter of this figure.

answer.short:
$16\,\mathrm{cm}$

Place the $2$ cm and $1$ cm squares along one side of the $3$ cm square, with the smaller squares touching.
answer.worked:
Place the $2$ cm and $1$ cm squares side by side along a side of the $3$ cm square. Their shared edges with the large square total $3$ cm, and their mutual shared edge is $1$ cm.
$$\begin{align*}P&=4(1+2+3)-2(3+1)\\P&=16\,\mathrm{cm}.\end{align*}$$
This is minimal: the $2$ cm square can share at most $2$ cm with the large square, and the $1$ cm square can share at most $1$ cm with each of the other two squares. Thus the total shared length cannot exceed $4$ cm.

spec.description: Authored solution arrangement showing three non-overlapping adjoining squares.
spec.mathematics: Square sides 3, 2 and 1 cm; total shared edge length 4 cm.
